issues.description: The problem tasks require ExcellenceLand to provide a method getRides(boolean filterActive) that returns only active rides when the flag is true. The solution repository implements getRides() with no boolean parameter (returns all rides) and the template does not provide the required method signature. This is a method-parameter mismatch between the problem specification and the provided solution/template and will confuse students about the exact API they must implement.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the ExcellenceLand API consistent with the problem statement: add a public method `public List<Ride> getRides(boolean filterActive)` (returning List<Ride>) in the template and solution. If the no-argument getRides() should be kept, provide it as an overload that delegates to the boolean-version. Update tests and documentation to reference the same signature.

issues.description: The problem statement requires filtering by "active rides" (getRides(boolean filterActive)) but the UML and implemented Ride class do not define any attribute or accessor that indicates whether a Ride is active (no boolean 'active' field or isActive() getter). Without such an attribute or method, students cannot implement the requested filtering behavior. This is a structural omission (missing attribute/accessor) across the artifacts.
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify and make explicit how a ride's "active" status is represented. Two options: (A) Add a private boolean attribute (e.g. `active`) to Ride, include it in the Ride constructor (respecting attribute ordering), and provide a public getter `public boolean isActive()`; then implement `getRides(boolean filterActive)` to filter by `isActive()`. Or (B) change the problem statement to remove the 'active' filtering requirement (or explain an alternative way to determine activity). Update UML, template, and solution consistently to reflect the chosen approach.

issues.description: The problem statement (task #3) requires ExcellenceLand to provide a method getRides(boolean filterActive) that — when filterActive is true — returns only active rides. The solution implementation instead provides a parameterless getRides() returning the raw List<Ride>. This is a signature/name mismatch for the same conceptual API: students reading the task expect to implement or call getRides(boolean), but the solution/template use/get a different method signature. The discrepancy creates mapping confusion about the required API and how to implement filtering (and will cause tests or student code that rely on the boolean parameter to fail).
issues.suggested_fix: Align the API across artifacts: change the ExcellenceLand implementation (and the template) to declare and implement public List<Ride> getRides(boolean filterActive). If filtering by "active" is intended, also ensure Ride exposes an appropriate boolean attribute/getter (e.g., private boolean active with public boolean isActive()) so the method can filter when filterActive==true. Alternatively, if no filtering is intended, update the problem statement to require getRides() (no parameter). Choose one consistent contract and apply it to problem, template, and solution.
